lines.text: Here's our robot, and a mark on the field, three meters away.
The job: drive to the mark, face the right way, and stop.
Stop exactly: within two centimeters, about a thumb's width, and within two degrees.
And fast, because every second of autonomous counts.
It might already be moving: sideways, or even the wrong way.
And the mark might move, as the robot learns where the target really is.
One piece of code handles all of this: Drive To Pose.
A pose is a spot on the field plus a direction to face: x, y, and heading.
We'll go in order: the goal, the idea in plain words, then the maths with real numbers.
Then the real Java, line by line, until you know why every line is there.
